title: Data Quality Report
description: The data quality report that gets read — versus the dimensions-of-DQ slide deck nobody opens. Five questions, answered specifically per data domain. The discipline is being honest about where the data is weak and quantifying the impact on downstream analysis.

worked_examples.content_md:
# Signups + Onboarding Events — Data Quality Report
_v0.1 · prepared by [DA] · 22 April 2026 · audience: data team + Marcelo (data eng) + Folake (CX, downstream consumer)_

## 1. What this report covers

- Tables: `users`, `onboarding_events`, `signup_channel_attribution`.
- Window assessed: 1 October 2025 – 21 April 2026.
- NOT in scope: billing / subscription data, third-party event sources.

## 2. What we found, ranked by impact

### Issue 1 (HIGH) — partner-channel attribution triple-counted between 18-25 March
- 3,127 user rows duplicated in the attribution table; downstream effect is overstated partner-channel signup volume.
- Affected: weekly partner-channel reporting; the £400k partner-referral business case modelling.
- Fix landed in the pipeline on 25 March; historical rows still need backfilling.

### Issue 2 (HIGH) — onboarding_step_completed event missing for ~14% of mobile signups
- Missing for a specific app build (v3.4.0–v3.4.2, ~6 weeks of releases) due to a client-side analytics bug.
- Affected: cohort completion-rate analyses; the simplified-onboarding churn analysis (already corrected for in the week-5 finding).
- Fixed in app v3.5; historical rows can't be recovered.

### Issue 3 (MEDIUM) — `signup_channel` field has 4% NULL rate
- Affects all rows where attribution can't be resolved (mostly direct-to-product visits with no UTM).
- Affected: any analysis sliced by channel.
- This is a fundamental ambiguity, not a bug — should be documented as 'unattributed' rather than fixed.

### Issue 4 (LOW) — three users have signed_up_at timestamps after their first event
- Likely race-condition between signup row insert and first event capture.
- Affected: edge cases in cohort definitions; will produce off-by-one-day cohort assignment for those three users.
- Acceptable as-is; the issue is rare enough that we'd lose more time fixing than we'd gain.

## 3. The numbers

| Issue | Rows affected | % of domain | Downstream metrics affected |
|-------|---------------|-------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | 3,127 | 18.3% (partner-channel slice) | weekly partner reporting, business case modelling |
| 2 | ~2,400 | 14.2% (mobile signups in window) | cohort completion-rate; simplified-onboarding analysis |
| 3 | ~840 | 4.1% (all signups) | any channel-sliced analysis |
| 4 | 3 | 0.02% | edge-case cohort assignment |

## 4. What we recommend

| Issue | Recommendation | Trade-off |
|-------|----------------|-----------|
| 1 | Backfill the affected attribution rows from raw event source (1 day eng work) | Two-week delay to clean partner-channel reporting if not done |
| 2 | Document the gap; do not attempt recovery (data not available) | Cohort analyses for the affected window have a known floor of completeness |
| 3 | Document 'unattributed' as a valid channel value; treat NULLs as unattributed in all transforms | Need to update three downstream dashboards |
| 4 | Accept and document | Minor cohort edge case in published analyses |

## 5. What we'd want to monitor going forward

- **dbt test on `signup_channel_attribution`:** uniqueness of `(user_id, attributed_at)` — would have flagged Issue 1 within 24 hours.
- **Mobile-build event-completeness check:** automated alert if `onboarding_step_completed` rate drops >5% week-on-week for any app version.
- **Schema-tracking on `signup_channel`:** new values appearing without our knowledge get flagged for triage.
- **Timestamp-ordering check:** assert `signed_up_at <= first_event_at` for each user; alert on violations beyond the known floor.

annotations.note: Issues ranked by impact, not by data-quality-framework category. 'Accuracy issue, severity HIGH' tells nobody anything. 'Partner-channel attribution triple-counted between 18-25 March, breaks partner-channel reporting + business case modelling' tells the reader what to act on.
Quantify everything. Row counts, percentages, named downstream metrics. Without numbers, the report reads as opinion. With numbers, it reads as a triage document the team can act on.
The fix-at-source / fix-in-transform / accept-and-document framing forces a real recommendation. 'Investigate further' is not a recommendation.
Monitoring checks live in dbt tests (or equivalent), not in a future-DA's head. The whole point of the DQ work is to prevent the next issue, not to catalogue the current one.

common_mistakes: Report written using the DAMA dimensions of data quality (accuracy / completeness / etc.) as the structure. Comprehensive and useless. Use impact-ranked issues instead.
Issues listed without quantifying downstream effect. The reader can't tell whether to act.
Recommendations of 'investigate further'. That's not a recommendation; that's a deferral. Make a call: fix at source, fix in transform, or accept-and-document.
DQ report produced once and never updated. The whole point is the ongoing health of the data; one-off reports become wallpaper.
Going to the data engineer with the report before having a conversation first. Same pattern as the bad-data scenario — the conversation comes before the document.
Listing every NULL value as an issue. NULLs that mean something specific (e.g. 'unattributed') are not data quality issues; they're modelling decisions.
variant_patterns: Pre-launch product variant: DQ report covers the new event schema only. Section 5 (monitoring) is the main deliverable — tests baked in before launch prevent the report from being needed in 6 months.
Regulatory-data variant: §6 'Regulatory implications' added at the end — which issues create audit risk, which create reporting accuracy risk, which create compliance breach risk.
Cross-source variant (data from multiple systems): §2 issues separately tagged by source system. Some issues are at the source; some are at the integration layer; the recommendations differ.
